title: Perfect Whole Roast Chicken

source.name: How To Roast a Whole Chicken - Garden in the Kitchen

ingredients.name: coarse kosher salt and black pepper

steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F (218°C). Pat chicken completely dry inside and out with paper towels.
Season the cavity with salt and pepper; stuff cavity with lemon halves, halved garlic head, and fresh rosemary/thyme sprigs.
Gently separate skin from breast meat with fingers and rub half the softened butter directly under the skin.
Rub remaining butter and olive oil all over the outside skin; season liberally with smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.
Place chicken breast-side up on a rack in a roasting pan (or over a bed of onions and potatoes).
Roast for 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 25 minutes until an instant-read thermometer reads 165°F in the thickest part of the breast and innermost thigh, and juices run clear.
Transfer chicken to a carving board and rest loosely tented with foil for 15 minutes before carving.
swaps: Can roast over chopped carrots and baby potatoes for a full sheet pan meal; garlic powder can replace fresh.
notes: Drying skin thoroughly and rubbing butter under the skin guarantees crispy crackling skin and succulent meat.

title: Crispy Baked Chicken Thighs

source.name: Baked Chicken Thighs (Crispy and Juicy!) | Downshiftology

steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F (205°C) and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Pat chicken thighs completely dry with paper towels on both sides.
Rub thighs with olive oil.
In a small dish, mix garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, oregano, thyme, salt, and pepper into a spice rub.
Season chicken thighs generously on all sides with the spice rub.
Place thighs skin-side up on the baking sheet with space between them.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy, and internal temperature reads 175°F to 180°F.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
swaps: Can use bone-in drumsticks; Italian seasoning can substitute for oregano/thyme.
notes: Cooking thighs to 175°F–180°F melts connective tissue and renders fat, yielding shatter-crisp skin.

title: Air Fryer Crispy (Un)Fried Chicken

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken breasts, sliced into tenders

steps: In a shallow bowl, whisk egg with 1 tablespoon water. In a second bowl, combine panko, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Dip each chicken tender first into egg wash, then press into seasoned panko until thoroughly coated.
Preheat air fryer to 390°F (200°C) for 3 minutes. Lightly spray basket with oil.
Arrange chicken tenders in a single uncrowded layer in the basket. Spray tops lightly with cooking spray.
Air-fry for 12 to 14 minutes, flipping halfway through, until coating is deeply golden and chicken reaches 165°F internal temperature.
Serve hot with favorite dipping sauce.
swaps: Can use chicken cutlets or bone-in pieces (increase cooking time to 20-22 minutes for bone-in).
notes: Delivers the crunch and satisfaction of fried chicken with minimal oil and fat.

title: Grilled Lemon Rosemary Chicken Breast
steps: Place chicken breasts between plastic wrap and gently pound thickest ends with a meat mallet to a uniform 3/4-inch thickness.
In a shallow dish, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, lemon zest, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, salt, and pepper.
Add chicken breasts, turning to coat; marinate in refrigerator for 15 to 30 minutes.
Preheat grill or grill pan to medium-high heat (approx. 400°F). Lightly oil grates.
Remove chicken from marinade, discarding excess liquid. Grill chicken for 5 to 6 minutes on the first side.
Flip chicken and grill for another 4 to 5 minutes until internal temperature reaches exactly 165°F and clear juices run.
Transfer to a plate, tent loosely with foil, and rest for 5 minutes before slicing.
swaps: Can use boneless chicken thighs (grill 6-7 minutes per side); fresh oregano can replace rosemary.
notes: Pounding breasts to an even thickness ensures uniform cooking without drying out the edges.

title: Savory Chicken Lo Mein with Vegetables

source.name: ENGLISH - Boston.gov
source.location: Boston Eats Community Recipes - Chicken Lo Mein, Page 35

ingredients.name: boneless chicken breast, sliced into thin strips
lo mein egg noodles or spaghetti
toasted sesame oil or vegetable oil

steps: Cook noodles in boiling water according to package directions until tender; drain and rinse with cold water.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Add sliced chicken strips and stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes until cooked through (165°F); remove to a plate.
Add remaining oil to wok with minced garlic and ginger, stir-frying for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Toss in broccoli florets, bell pepper, and shredded carrots, stir-frying for 3 minutes until crisp-tender.
Whisk together soy sauce and oyster sauce in a small bowl.
Add cooked noodles, cooked chicken, and sauce to wok, tossing vigorously over high heat for 2 minutes until hot and evenly glazed.
swaps: Can use chicken thighs; snap peas, cabbage, or mushrooms can replace broccoli.
notes: Fast 25-minute weeknight dinner combining lean protein, colorful vegetables, and tender noodles.

title: Creamy Tuscan Garlic Chicken

source.name: 50 Side Dishes for Chicken - A Couple Cooks

ingredients.name: sun-dried tomatoes in oil, drained and chopped

steps: Season chicken cutlets on both sides with Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken for 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (165°F); transfer to a plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic and sun-dried tomatoes to pan drippings, cooking for 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth and heavy cream, bringing to a simmer for 2 minutes.
Add fresh spinach and parmesan cheese, stirring until spinach wilts into the creamy sauce.
Return chicken cutlets to skillet, spooning warm sauce over top, and simmer for 2 minutes before serving.
swaps: Can serve over penne pasta, rice, or mashed potatoes; chicken tenders can replace cutlets.
notes: One-skillet Italian bistro favorite that combines savory pan-seared chicken with creamy garlic sauce.

title: Restaurant-Quality Cast-Iron Seared Chicken Breast

source.name: The Best Chicken Breast You'll Ever Make | Epicurious 101

ingredients.name: high-heat neutral oil (avocado or light olive oil)
kosher salt and cracked black pepper

steps: Pound chicken breasts gently between parchment paper to a uniform 3/4-inch thickness. Pat completely dry with paper towels.
Season generously on both sides with kosher salt and black pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add chicken breasts and sear undisturbed for 4 to 5 minutes until a deep golden-brown crust forms.
Flip breasts. Add butter, smashed garlic, and fresh thyme sprigs to the skillet.
Tilt pan and continuously spoon foaming herb butter over the breasts for 3 to 4 minutes until internal temperature reaches exactly 165°F.
Transfer chicken to a warm cutting board and rest for 3 to 5 minutes before slicing against the grain.
swaps: Can use rosemary instead of thyme; lemon slices can be added to the foaming butter.
notes: Pounding to uniform thickness and continuous butter-basting guarantees juicy chicken breasts every time.

title: Moroccan Braised Chicken Stew with Chickpeas

source.name: Recipes - The Nutrition Source | Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health

ingredients.name: bone-in chicken thighs or drumsticks, skin removed

steps: Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown chicken thighs on both sides for 5 minutes; transfer to a plate.
Add chopped onion, garlic, and grated ginger to pot, cooking for 3 minutes until softened.
Stir in cumin, coriander, cinnamon, salt, and pepper, toasting spices for 1 minute.
Add diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and drained chickpeas, stirring to combine.
Return chicken to pot, bringing liquid to a simmer. Cover, reduce heat to low, and braise for 30 minutes until chicken is tender and reaches 175°F.
Stir in fresh cilantro and ladle over warm couscous or brown rice.
swaps: Can add dried apricots or raisins for traditional Moroccan sweetness; butternut squash cubes can be added.
notes: Aromatic tagine-style chicken stew packed with fiber-rich chickpeas and warm Mediterranean spices.

title: Roman-Style Chicken with Peppers and Prosciutto

source.name: Our 50 Most-Popular Healthy Recipes - Food Network

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken breasts or thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
bell peppers (red and yellow), thinly sliced

steps: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Season chicken with salt and pepper; cook for 5 minutes until browned, then remove to a plate.
Add remaining oil to pan. Sauté chopped prosciutto, sliced bell peppers, and onion for 5 minutes until tender.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in white wine, scraping up browned bits, and simmer for 2 minutes until reduced by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, capers, and oregano.
Return chicken to skillet, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes until chicken is tender and cooked through (165°F).
Serve warm with crusty bread or over pasta.
swaps: Can omit prosciutto or use bacon; serve over polenta instead of crusty bread.
notes: Saucy, flavorful Italian comfort dish that reheats beautifully for leftovers.

title: Aunt Elizabeth's Chicken Paprikash
steps: Melt butter in a heavy Dutch oven over medium heat. Brown chicken pieces for 4 to 5 minutes per side, then remove to a plate.
Add diced onions to the pot, cooking slowly over medium-low heat for 10 minutes until soft, sweet, and golden.
Remove pot from heat and stir in sweet Hungarian paprika and garlic (removing from heat prevents paprika from scorching and turning bitter).
Return pot to heat, pour in chicken broth, and return chicken pieces to the pot.
Cover and simmer gently over low heat for 30 minutes until chicken is tender and registers 175°F.
In a small bowl, whisk sour cream with flour and 2 tablespoons of warm cooking liquid.
Stir sour cream mixture into simmering sauce, cooking for 2 minutes until sauce is smooth and velvety.
Serve hot ladled over generous bowls of buttered egg noodles.
swaps: Can use Greek yogurt instead of sour cream; nokedli (dumplings) or mashed potatoes can replace egg noodles.
notes: Authentic paprikash relies on slow-caramelized onions and authentic Hungarian paprika; never burn the paprika.
